evidence.note: Built an independent reference (ref.py) and later an authoritative fp64 reference (test_fp64.py) that is re-run as a frozen correctness baseline throughout — the explicit 'reference matches math' milestone.
Wrote test_full.py for 'Full domain correctness' and stress-tested N=2048 across seeds, establishing a correct-across-the-grid milestone with a concrete done-check before any timing.

Deep numeric investigation on the hardest cases (bf16/fp32/tf32 accuracy, NaN/inf, large N=2048, fp64 comparison) happens BEFORE benchmarking — risk-sequenced correctness on the toughest numerics first.
Latency work (bench.py, 10-shape benchmark) begins only after correctness established — performance is a distinct track gated on the correct baseline.
Optimization decomposed into many isolated prototype kernels (proto_pg, proto_bmm, proto_of, proto_front, etc.), each independently benchmarked/tuned per-shape, rather than one monolithic fused push.
A fused optimization fails correctness (step 343), failing cases are isolated (345), and the change is reverted (353) — per-milestone checks catching a fast-but-wrong regression before it sticks.

reasoning: The trajectory exhibits clean correctness-first staging: an independent then fp64 reference oracle (12,114), a full-domain correctness milestone (38-39,118), and only then a separate latency-optimization track (81+), with the frozen fp64 baseline re-verified after every significant kernel change (111,321,343,414,529,628). This exceeds the level-8 anchor's ordered-milestones-with-exit-tests, adding risk-sequencing (hardest N=2048/Cauchy/precision numerics nailed first, 42-79) and a heavily decomposed optimization stage (dozens of per-kernel/per-shape prototypes) with per-milestone checks that catch and revert a fast-but-wrong regression (343-353). It falls just short of a perfect 10 because the risk-sequencing appears partly reactive to discovered numeric failures rather than pre-planned.
